note: What this is. A reference 23s9p module (one of four in a Tesla Model Y 4680 pack) filled with BYD FC4680 LFP cells. Each cell has an OCV, a series resistance and one RC branch (cell-to-cell spread 1 % in capacity, 3 % in resistance), and two thermal nodes (core and can) cooled by serpentine ribbons. The 9 cells of a group are solved in parallel, so a short drains its whole group. The group voltages are shown as a cell monitor would measure them (0.3 mV noise, 0.1 mV resolution, 1 Hz); at cell level, an impedance-based temperature per cell (0.5 K noise at 1 Hz, 1 K calibration bias, averaged over 10 s). Inside a shorted cell, the hottest point comes from the 3-D cell twin of paper 1.2: the short's power history convolved with the unit response of its library, scaled for the footprint. The cut-open view shows that peak on an illustrative field shape. The detector (Physics AI NN) sees only the BMS signals. Not modelled: escalation of a short; shorts above 4 W are flagged as beyond soft-short scope. Ribbon conductance is an estimate.
